source.publication: 2025 Modification Worksheet: Taxable Social Security Income Worksheet (booklet page 18)
source.section: Worksheet Step 1 lines 1-7, Step 2 lines 8-13 and instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1s; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 70,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 95,500.00. Federal taxable income = 95,500.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65+ = 62,400.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 95,500.00. Line 1s, Social Security worksheet: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70), person 1 born 1962-06-15 (age 63). Line 3 federal AGI 95,500.00; line 4 Married filing jointly; line 5 born on or before 03/01/1959: yes; line 6 133,750.00; line 7 95,500.00 less than 133,750.00: yes. Line 8 benefits 30,000.00; line 9 attributed to the person born on or before 03/01/1959 0.00; line 10 = 0.0000; line 12 = 0.0000. Line 11 taxable benefits 25,500.00; line 13 = 25,500.00 x 0.0000 = 0.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 95,500.00 + (0.00) = 95,500.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 95,500.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 21,800.00 (Married filing jointly). Line 5 = 95,500.00 - 21,800.00 = 73,700.00. Line 6 exemptions: 2 x 5,100.00 = 10,200.00. Line 7 taxable income = 73,700.00 - 10,200.00 = 63,500.00. Line 8 tax on 63,500.00 by the schedule as numbers: 63,500.00 x 0.0375 = 2381.250000 = 2,381.25. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 2,381.25. Note: Line 5 passes because the older spouse qualifies, but all the benefits belong to the spouse under full retirement age: line 9 is zero, so the modification is zero.
accepted_approximations: On a joint return with one qualifying person, the Social Security subtraction is the taxable benefits times that person's share of total benefits (worksheet lines 8-12). Consumers must divide taxable Social Security between the spouses by their gross benefits to get this result.
